sections.overview: This bowerbird is endemic to Queensland’s Wet Tropics in Australia.
sections.identification: Both sexes have a notched, tooth-like bill; males use it to cut leaves.
sections.habitat: It lives mainly in upland rainforest, with some display sites in regrowth forest.
sections.diet: It eats fruit and leaves, with leaves especially important when fruit is scarce.
sections.behavior: Males clear and decorate ground courts with fresh leaves for display.
sections.reproduction: The female lays one or two eggs in a cup nest placed high in tangled vines.
sections.ecology: Males disperse seeds in piles beneath their favoured calling perches after eating fleshy fruits.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists it as Near Threatened (2022), with climate change a suspected ongoing pressure.
